# Write-Only Code

**Source:** [Write-Only Code](https://www.heavybit.com/library/article/write-only-code) - Joseph Ruscio, General Partner at Heavybit, February 2026

## Summary

"Write-Only Code" describes an emerging paradigm where substantial amounts of production code are generated by AI agents and never read by humans. Rather than treating this as a failure mode, Ruscio frames it as an inevitable evolution: "humans had to read this" becomes an anti-pattern as organizations develop new mechanisms for trust and accountability that don't depend on manual code review.

## Historical Context: Breaking Bottlenecks

Ruscio draws parallels to previous infrastructure revolutions. When cloud computing eliminated hardware provisioning constraints, developer velocity became the new bottleneck. Now, AI elimination of coding work itself represents the next threshold shift. Each revolution removes the current constraint and reveals the next one.

## From Review to Trust

Instead of relying on human code inspection, organizations will develop new confidence mechanisms:

- **Code reading coverage** - Metrics tracking what percentage of production code humans have actually examined, acknowledging that 100% is no longer realistic or necessary
- **Slop radius management** - Understanding how far unintended behaviors can propagate through a system before being caught
- **Automation-based confidence** - Replacing manual review with automated verification systems (tests, formal methods, runtime monitoring) as the primary trust mechanism

## Engineer Role Transformation

Rather than authors and reviewers, engineers become:

- **Systems designers** - Shaping high-level intent and constraints that guide AI code generation
- **Trade-off managers** - Balancing competing priorities across systems rather than within individual functions
- **Risk reducers** - Building systems that remain correct without requiring comprehensive human understanding of every line

## Core Insight

> "The role of a software engineer has always been to sit between poorly specified, natural-language business goals and mostly deterministic machine behavior."

Responsibility doesn't disappear when code becomes write-only. It evolves toward designing self-correcting systems rather than reviewing every line. The engineer's value shifts from "can write and read code" to "can design systems where correctness is verifiable without reading every line."

## Implications

The challenge isn't whether write-only code arrives, but whether organizations will invest early in new primitives for trust, accountability, and control, or adapt haphazardly under pressure.

This connects to several related concepts in AI engineering:

- **Backpressure for agents** - Write-only code demands stronger automated feedback loops (tests, type systems, linters) since human review is no longer the safety net
- **Context rot** - As codebases grow with AI-generated code, the volume of context that would need to be reviewed exceeds what models (or humans) can reliably process
- **The Bitter Lesson** - General methods (automated verification, runtime monitoring) will outperform human-knowledge approaches (manual code review) as scale increases

## Key Takeaway

Human accountability endures; the mechanisms ensuring it fundamentally change. Organizations that build robust automated verification systems early will thrive in a write-only code world, while those clinging to human review as the sole gatekeeper will be overwhelmed by the volume of AI-generated code.
